original_question: What geometric regularity can the boundary components of a Herman ring have? In particular, under what hypotheses are these boundaries Jordan curves or quasicircles, when can they have fractal structure, what can be said about their Hausdorff dimension or Lebesgue measure, and can a Herman-ring boundary ever have positive area?
target_in_paper: Section 6 (Conclusion), item 4 of the unnumbered list of open problems: the geometric nature of the boundary components of Herman rings.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's intended open problem. It correctly centers on boundary components of a Herman ring and explicitly includes every issue named in the paper's formulation: Jordan-curve regularity, quasicircle regularity, possible fractal structure, Hausdorff dimension, Lebesgue measure, and the possibility of positive area.
missing_details: The paper's ambient setting is that f is either a rational map of degree at least 2 on the Riemann sphere or a transcendental meromorphic function on the complex plane; throughout the survey these are grouped under the term 'meromorphic'.
A Herman ring H is a doubly connected periodic Fatou component, so the relevant 'boundary components' are the connected components of ∂H, and there are exactly two of them.
The paper presents this as an open research direction in the conclusion, not as a numbered theorem or conjecture with explicit hypotheses.

The paper begins with 'boundary components' but phrases the quantitative part for the boundary of the Herman ring itself: the Hausdorff dimension and Lebesgue measure of ∂H, and whether ∂H can have positive area.
No additional hypotheses are built into the paper's statement; the unknown is precisely which conditions, if any, force Jordan-curve or quasicircle boundaries or allow fractal geometry.

There are no extra algebraic parameters to specify here (such as homogeneity, nilpotency, or asymptotic quantifiers like 'for all sufficiently large m'); the missing stand-alone details are the dynamical setting and the exact meaning of 'boundary components'.
If one wants paper-faithful terminology, the paper also uses 'a connected component of the boundary of a Herman ring' as the precise boundary-component language.
refined_question: Let f be either a rational map of degree at least 2 on the Riemann sphere or a transcendental meromorphic function on the complex plane, and let H be a Herman ring of f (so H is a doubly connected periodic Fatou component with two connected boundary components). Determine the possible geometry of the connected components of ∂H: under what conditions are they Jordan curves or quasicircles, when can they instead have fractal structure, what can be said about the Hausdorff dimension and Lebesgue measure of ∂H, and can ∂H have positive area?
justification: The draft clearly targets the fourth unnumbered open problem in Section 6. That passage is the nearest official formulation in the paper and is almost a line-by-line paraphrase of your draft. Section 1 supplies the ambient class of maps and the fact that a Herman ring is doubly connected, while Section 4.1, Lemma 4.1, confirms that the paper uses 'connected component of the boundary of a Herman ring' as the precise notion of boundary component. So the main refinement needed is to make the ambient dynamical setting and the boundary terminology explicit without broadening the scope beyond the paper's actual open problem.
